title: Can You Handle the Tracking Error? | Dimensional
gist: Dimensional argues that small-cap, value, high-profitability stocks have earned 17.1% annualized versus 10.9% for the US market since 1963, but with 11.8% tracking error and a worst 36-month underperformance of over 72 points, so they work best as a tilt within a diversified portfolio.

insights.claim: US small value high-profitability stocks returned 17.1% annualized from July 1963 to July 2026 versus 10.9% for the broad US market, enough to double money roughly every four years instead of seven.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
entities: US small value high profitability stocks
Fama/French Total US Market Research Index
insights.so_what: The historical premium case for concentrating in small, cheap, profitable stocks.

insights.claim: Stocks that are simultaneously small cap, low price-to-book and highly profitable are rare and a tiny part of the market, which produces extreme deviations from market returns.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Small opportunity set makes a pure-play portfolio concentrated and volatile.

insights.claim: The small value high-profitability group has an annualized tracking error of 11.8% and at its worst underperformed the market by over 72 percentage points over a 36-month period.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
entities: US small value high profitability stocks
insights.so_what: Investors must be able to stomach multi-year underperformance to capture the premium.
insights.quote: underperformed the market by over 72 percentage points in a 36-month period

insights.claim: The practical approach is to tilt a broadly diversified allocation toward higher-expected-return stocks rather than hold only factor-concentrated stocks.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
insights.so_what: Use factor tilts as a seasoning within diversification, sized to tracking-error tolerance.
